Ingredients (one per line):
1¾ cups flour
⅔ cup sugar
2 tsp. baking powder
½ tsp. baking soda
¼ tsp. salt
1 cup mashed banana (3 ripe medium bananas)
⅓ cup margarine, butter or shortening
2 Tbsp. milk
2 eggs
¼ cup chopped nuts
Instructions (one step per line):
Preheat oven to 350°. Grease bread loaf pan.
In a large mixer bowl combine 1 cup of the flour, the sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt.
Add mashed banana; margarine, butter or shortening; and milk. Beat with an electric mixer on low speed till blended, then on high speed for 2 minutes.
Add eggs and remaining flour; beat till blended.
Stir in nuts.
Pour batter into a greased 8x4x2 inch loaf pan. Bake in a 350° oven for 55 to 60 minutes or till toothpick inserted near the center comes out clean.
Cool for 10 minutes on a wire rack. Remove from pan; cool thoroughly on a wire rack.

Ingredients (one per line):
1½ cups wheat bran
1 cup soured milk (1 tsp. lemon juice plus milk to make 1 cup; let stand 5 minutes)
⅓ cup vegetable oil
1 egg
⅔ cup brown sugar
½ tsp. vanilla
1 cup flour
1 tsp. baking soda
1 tsp. baking powder
½ tsp. salt
½ cup raisins (optional)
Instructions (one step per line):
Preheat oven to 375°.
Mix bran and soured milk in large bowl. Let stand for 10 minutes.
Beat oil, egg, brown sugar and vanilla. Mix into bran mixture.
Add dry ingredients and mix well.
Grease 12 muffin cups. Scoop evenly into cups.
Bake for 20 minutes. Remove from cups to cool completely.

Ingredients (one per line):
1¼ cups flour
¾ cup corn meal
¼ cup sugar
2 tsp. baking powder
½ tsp. salt
1 cup milk
¼ cup oil
1 beaten egg
Instructions (one step per line):
Preheat oven to 400°. Grease 8" or 9" pan.
Combine dry ingredients.
Stir milk, oil and egg together and add to dry ingredients. Stir just until dry ingredients are moistened.
Spread into prepared pan.
Bake 20 – 25 minutes or until light brown and toothpick tests clean.
Notes & tips: Variation: double the recipe and use a 9x13 pan.

Ingredients (one per line):
1½ cups milk
¾ cup sugar
½ cup butter (or margarine)
2 Tbsp. yeast
2 cups warm water (I use hot out of the faucet)
1 Tbsp. sugar
1 egg
1 Tbsp. salt
9-10 cups all-purpose flour
½ cup butter, melted (for brushing)
Instructions (one step per line):
Combine milk, sugar and ½ cup of butter in a microwave safe bowl; heat in the microwave for about 2 minutes or until butter is mostly melted.
In a measuring cup dissolve yeast in warm water and sugar. Let sit for a couple of minutes until bubbly and growing.
Stir into milk mixture 1-2 cups of the flour, then add egg and salt, and leave it to cool for just a couple of minutes. Add yeast mixture and stir well.
Gradually stir in the remaining cups of flour 2 cups at a time (9 – 10 cups total including the flour added in Step 3) with a wooden spoon or fork. Mix until it becomes necessary to incorporate the rest of the flour by hand.
Place smoothed dough covered in a greased bowl. Leave in a warm place and let rise for 45 – 60 minutes or until doubled in size.
Butter or spray with cooking spray two large cookie sheets.
Divide dough into 4 sections and roll one into a circle.
Melt ½ cup butter and brush the top from edge to edge.
Cut dough into quarters, then each quarter into three using a pizza cutter making 12 rolls.
Roll the dough starting with the wide end of the triangle. Tuck the tail of the triangle under the roll and place it on the buttered cookie sheet, 24 to a sheet.
Repeat with remaining 3 sections of dough, one at a time. Cover with greased plastic wrap and let rise to nearly double their size in a warm place.
Preheat oven to 350°F. Bake about 15 - 17 minutes or until golden brown.
For Cinnamon Rolls, after rolling a section of dough into a circle and brushing with butter, sprinkle generously with a cinnamon sugar mixture. Roll, let rise and bake. Pour Powdered Sugar Icing over top while still slightly warm.

Ingredients (one per line):
3 cups flour
1 tsp. salt
⅓ cup olive oil, plus more for rolling
1 cup warm water
Instructions (one step per line):
Mix flour and salt.
Add ⅓ cup oil and water and mix.
Knead for about 5 minutes.
Separate into 2 inch balls and roll balls in bowl of olive oil.
Place on pan and cover to rest.
Roll or press each ball when ready to cook as flat as possible into rounds.
Place on griddle or heated skillet and bake each side until desired browning occurs.
Place in stack on plate as each tortilla is done and cover with a wet rag.

Ingredients (one per line):
3½ to 3¾ cups all-purpose flour
2 Tbsp. sugar
½ tsp. salt
1 package active dry yeast (1 Tbsp.)
¼ cup margarine or butter
¾ cup milk
1 egg
¼ cup margarine or butter, melted
½ cup sugar
2 tsp. cinnamon
Frosting:
2 cups powdered sugar
½ tsp. vanilla
2 Tbsp. milk
Instructions (one step per line):
Preheat oven to 350°. Grease 12-cup bundt cake pan.
Mix 1½ cups of the flour, 2 tablespoons of sugar, salt and the yeast in a bowl.
Heat milk and ¼ cup margarine in a small saucepan until very warm (about 120°F). Add milk mixture and egg to flour mixture.
Beat on low speed for about 30 seconds and then on medium to high speed for 3 minutes. Stir in enough remaining flour to make dough easy to handle.
Turn out onto a floured surface and knead dough until smooth and elastic, about 5-6 minutes.
Melt butter. Quickly combine the ½ cup sugar and 2 tsp. cinnamon.
Shape dough into balls. Drop them into butter and then roll in sugar/cinnamon mixture and then into pan as they are complete. (This is NOT an exact science – balls do not need to be pretty and they are fine in pan as they fall!!!)
Bake until golden brown, 25 to 30 minutes. Cool 2 minutes; invert to heatproof serving plate.
Frosting: combine powdered sugar and vanilla. Add enough milk to make desired consistency. Mix well.

Ingredients (one per line):
1 package (1 Tbsp.) active dry yeast
3 cups warm water
6 Tbsp. shortening
2 Tbsp. sugar
2 tsp. salt
6 Tbsp. nonfat dry milk
6½ cups flour
Oil for frying
Instructions (one step per line):
In a large bowl, dissolve yeast in warm water.
Add shortening, sugar, salt, and dry milk.
Stir in flour to make a soft dough. Mix well.
Knead dough 15 to 20 minutes; set aside to rest for 10 minutes.
Roll dough to ¼-inch thickness; cut in squares or triangles.
Fry, turning once, in hot fat until lightly browned on each side.

Ingredients (one per line):
3 cups all-purpose flour
2 tsp. ground cinnamon
1 tsp. baking soda
¼ tsp. salt
½ tsp. baking powder
½ tsp. ground nutmeg
2 cups sugar
2 cups finely shredded unpeeled zucchini
½ cup cooking oil
2 eggs
½ tsp. finely shredded lemon peel
1 cup chopped walnuts
Instructions (one step per line):
In a large bowl combine flour, cinnamon, baking soda, salt, baking powder, and nutmeg.
In another mixing bowl combine sugar, shredded zucchini, cooking oil, eggs, and lemon peel; mix well.
Add flour mixture; stir just till combined.
Stir in chopped walnuts.
Pour batter into 2 greased 8x4x2-inch loaf pans.
Bake in a 350° oven for 55 to 60 minutes or till a toothpick inserted near the center comes out clean.
Cool for 10 minutes on a wire rack.
Remove bread from the pan; cool thoroughly on a wire rack.

Ingredients (one per line):
1 cup (2 sticks) butter, softened
1 cup sugar
1 cup brown sugar
1 tsp. baking soda
1 tsp. baking powder
1 tsp. salt
1 tsp. vanilla
2 eggs
3½ cups flour
1 cup chocolate chips, or as many as desired
Instructions (one step per line):
Preheat oven to 350°.
Cream together butter and sugars.
Add baking soda, baking powder, salt, and vanilla and beat until combined.
Add eggs one at a time, beating after each addition just until combined.
Add flour and mix well.
Add chocolate chips.
Place on ungreased cookie sheet and bake at 350° for 8 – 10 minutes.
